name: flow_level
meaning: How vehicles load the network: 0 free flow (no vehicle affects another), 2 the point queue (queues form at capacity but take no road space, so nothing spills back), 3 a spatial queue, 4 the full triangular fundamental diagram, with spillback, turn pockets and en-route rerouting.
source: A choice of model, not a calibrated value.

name: flow_step_s
meaning: The loading's step at flow levels 2 to 4, in seconds: a bookkeeping boundary at which links forget what they no longer need; no vehicle's timing depends on it.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: window
meaning: The simulation window's length when `window` is not given: the run starts at the earliest departure, rounded down to the quarter hour, and stops this many hours later. Trips departing outside the window are left out with a `WindowWarning`; trips still under way at its end are unfinished.
source: A setting: the starter cases' morning departures span three hours.

name: default_weight
meaning: How many people one simulated traveller stands for, for a trip whose row gives no weight: 1 simulates everyone; more is faster and coarser.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: master_seed
meaning: The one number every random stream starts from (who chooses again, which alternative a sampled choice model draws): the same seed reproduces a run. A whole number from 0 to 2^64 − 1.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: choice_detour_limit
meaning: A traveller is offered a route only if its expected time, at the last loading's times (free flow at first), is at most this share above the best route's: 0.5 offers routes at most 50 % slower. 0 offers every route of the set. The best route is always offered; with mode choice the limit applies within each mode.
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: choice_max_routes
meaning: The most routes a traveller is offered: the fastest at their departure among those within `choice_detour_limit`; 0 offers every route within the limit. A pair's set may hold more (`route_update` `max_routes`).
source: An assumption on the size of a consideration set: Prato (2009), Route choice modeling: past, present and future research directions, Journal of Choice Modelling 2(1) 65–100, https://doi.org/10.1016/S1755-5345(13)70005-8, reviews choice sets of a handful of routes.

name: max_cost_vectors
meaning: The most coefficient vectors route searches are made by. Every route search minimises the choice model's link-additive utility: the travel time plus the seconds-equivalent of every per-link term it weighs (length, running cost, tolls, user link values, for bikes the kilometres by facility). A user class whose coefficients on those terms differ from another's gets its own search trees, up to this many; beyond it, a class is searched by the kept class's nearest by value of time (a `cost_vectors_grouped` diagnostic). Where the utility weighs time alone every search is by time and this changes nothing.
source: A setting of the computation (each vector costs about one more set of search trees per loading); uncalibrated.

name: hub_join_m
meaning: How far a parking may be from a stop, in metres in a straight line, to join the stop's hub in the outputs (`hub_id`) when its table names none; an argument of `Scenario.run`. Results do not depend on it, so it is not in the fingerprint.
source: An assumption: a short walk across a station's forecourt. Uncalibrated.

name: bike_dedicated_km_h
meaning: A bike's speed on a painted lane, cycle street or separate track, in km/h; never above the link's speed limit.
source: An assumption: 20 % above the mixed-traffic speed, for fewer stops and conflicts. On a Bologna street cyclists slowed about 20 % on a separated facility against 40 % in mixed traffic: Bernardi, Krizek and Rupi (2016), Journal of Transport and Land Use, https://jtlu.org/index.php/jtlu/article/view/715

name: bike_lane_cost_factor
meaning: With `bike_cost="dedicated"`, multiplies the travel time of a bike link with a painted lane (or a cycle street) when bike routes are searched, against 1 on a separate track; 1 counts a lane as a track.
source: Uncalibrated. In Portland painted lanes were no more attractive than a quiet street while off-street paths were valued highly (Broach, Dill and Gliebe 2012, Transportation Research Part A 46(10) 1730–1740, https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/transa/v46y2012i10p1730-1740.html); a value between 1 and `bike_mixed_cost_factor` is to be taken from such a model.

name: bike_mixed_cost_factor
meaning: With `bike_cost="dedicated"` (the default), multiplies the travel time of every bike link without a lane or track (ferries excepted) when bike routes are searched, so cyclists accept a detour to ride on dedicated infrastructure; the time ridden is unchanged. No effect with `bike_cost="time"`.
source: An assumption, a placeholder until a value is taken from a route choice model. Cyclists valued off-street paths highly in Portland (Broach, Dill and Gliebe 2012, Transportation Research Part A 46(10) 1730–1740, https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/transa/v46y2012i10p1730-1740.html) and appeared indifferent to separate paths in Amsterdam's inner city (Ton, Cats, Duives and Hoogendoorn 2017, Transportation Research Record 2662 75–82, https://doi.org/10.3141/2662-09).

name: bike_mixed_km_h
meaning: A bike's speed in mixed traffic, stops included, in km/h; never above the link's speed limit.
source: About 15 km/h is the urban average in the Netherlands, stop time included: de Hartog, Boogaard, Nijland and Hoek, Environmental Health Perspectives, 2011, the authors' response in the correspondence on their 2010 paper, https://doi.org/10.1289/ehp.0901747.

name: busway.free_flow_km_h
meaning: Free-flow speed of a busway (buses only: `highway=busway`, or a road closed to other motor traffic but open to buses) where the data gives no `maxspeed`, in km/h; every speed is then multiplied by `free_flow_speed_factor`. A higher speed shortens free-flow times and, with capacity and jam density, changes the backward wave speed.
source: An assumption: a secondary road's speed, buses running at urban arterial speeds.

name: busway.jam_density_veh_km_lane
meaning: Jam density of a busway (buses only: `highway=busway`, or a road closed to other motor traffic but open to buses): vehicles (PCU) per km and lane at a standstill, so how many vehicles a link stores. With the free-flow speed v and capacity q it sets the backward wave speed, w = q / (k_j − q/v). Multiplied by `jam_density_factor`.
source: An assumption: a secondary road's row.

name: busway.lanes
meaning: Lanes per direction of a busway (buses only: `highway=busway`, or a road closed to other motor traffic but open to buses) where the data gives no lane count. Capacity and storage (jam density) are per lane, so both scale with it; turn pockets need two lanes or more.
source: An assumption: a secondary road's row.

name: busway.saturation_flow_veh_h_lane
meaning: Capacity per lane of a busway (buses only: `highway=busway`, or a road closed to other motor traffic but open to buses), in vehicles (PCU) per hour, where the data states no capacity; times the lanes it is the link's capacity, then multiplied by `capacity_factor`. At a signal it is capped by the speed band (`street_30`, `street_50`, `street_70`).
source: An assumption: a secondary road's row.

name: capacity_factor
meaning: Multiplies every road link's capacity, including a capacity the data states, after the signal speed bands' cap.
source: A calibration factor; 1 leaves the shipped table unchanged.

name: control_delay_factor
meaning: Multiplies the constant control delay added to the free-flow time of every link that ends at a signal.
source: A calibration factor; 1 leaves the shipped table unchanged.

name: signal_degree_of_saturation
meaning: The degree of saturation at which each signalised approach's constant control delay is computed by Webster's uniform delay, d = 0.5 · C · (1 − g/C)² / (1 − x · g/C): about 21 s at the defaults. The delay does not respond to the flow a run produces. From 0 to 1.
source: The uniform-delay term of Webster (1958), Traffic signal settings, Road Research Technical Paper 39 (HMSO), as Akgungor and Bullen's review of delay models describes it, https://nacto.org/wp-content/uploads/analytical_delay_models_for_signalized_intersections_akgungor.pdf (the 1958 paper itself was not read); the degree of saturation 0.85 is an assumption.

name: signal_green_fraction
meaning: The effective green time as a share of the cycle on every signalised approach: a turn out of such an approach gets this share of its saturation flow, and it enters the control delay. From 0 to 1.
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: signal_merge_m
meaning: How far from a junction, along its street, an OpenStreetMap signal belongs to that junction, in metres. A signal without traffic_signals:direction on a street within this distance of a junction (a stop line) stops only the traffic heading into the junction, not the traffic just leaving it on the far side; a junction tagged within this distance behind a stop line or another signalised junction adds no second delay. A signal farther from every junction (a mid-block crossing) stops both directions. 0 turns the rule off. Read when a network is read from OpenStreetMap.
source: An assumption: a stop line lies a few metres to about 20 m before a junction's centre; the OpenStreetMap wiki asks for the signal on the junction's node or on each approach's stop line, https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:highway%3Dtraffic_signals

name: street_30.saturation_flow_veh_h_lane

The speed is the link's `maxspeed`, else its class's. Not applied to a link whose capacity the data states, nor to unsignalised approaches.
source: CEREMA (2016), Débit de saturation aux carrefours à feux : note de synthèse, table 2, https://cerema.fr/fr/system/files/documents/2017/10/cerema_pcitcv_oct2016_note_synthese_debit_saturation_cle76df75.pdf; CROW publication 328, Handboek wegontwerp (2013), as a municipal traffic study applies it, https://www.ruimtelijkeplannen.nl/documents/NL.IMRO.0632.Vanzwietenweg-bOW1/b_NL.IMRO.0632.Vanzwietenweg-bOW1_tb15.pdf (the handbook itself was not read). source: An assumption: common OpenStreetMap speed conventions where `maxspeed` is absent.

name: tertiary.jam_density_veh_km_lane
meaning: Jam density of a `tertiary` road: vehicles (PCU) per km and lane at a standstill, so how many vehicles a link stores. With the free-flow speed v and capacity q it sets the backward wave speed, w = q / (k_j − q/v). Multiplied by `jam_density_factor`.
source: Within the 120–200 vehicles per km and lane estimated, 140–160 called most realistic, by Helbing (2001), Reviews of Modern Physics 73(4) 1067–1141, https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/0012229 (p. 9).

name: tertiary.lanes

name: priority
meaning: 1 turns on priority at unsignalised merges: a vehicle gives way to the first vehicle at the downstream end of an approach of higher road class (or of the same class and at least 1.5 times the capacity) bound for the same link, and a departing vehicle gives way to every approach. 0 or 1.
source: openmobisim's own remedy for loops of links that lock (uncalibrated). Off by default: with one first-in-first-out queue per link, a vehicle giving way holds up everything behind it.

name: reroute
meaning: 1 turns on en-route rerouting: a vehicle blocked at the downstream end of its link for `reroute_after_s` re-routes from where it is. 0 or 1. Unsaid, it is on at flow levels 3 and 4 and off at level 2, where nothing waits for room.
source: openmobisim's own remedy for loops of links that lock (uncalibrated): drivers who change course escape a locked loop.

name: reroute_after_s
meaning: How long a vehicle waits, blocked at the downstream end of its link, before it re-routes, in seconds.
source: Uncalibrated; no observed diversion delay was found. MATSim's stuck time defaults to 30 s (Mersini and Ziemke, MATSim User Meeting 2025, slide 6, https://matsim.org/conferences/mum2025/presentations/mersini.pdf); Olmos et al. (2018), PNAS 115(50) 12654–12661, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6294880, let a vehicle stopped about two minutes re-route.

name: reroute_max
meaning: The most times one trip re-routes.
source: An assumption: three, to keep a vehicle from wandering.

name: reroute_min_gain
meaning: How much faster the new route must be than the rest of the current one, by the costs the vehicle sees, as a share, for a vehicle to re-route.
source: Uncalibrated. A relative threshold of this kind is the indifference band of boundedly rational route switching (Mahmassani and Jayakrishnan 1991, Transportation Research Part A 25(5) 293–307, https://doi.org/10.1016/0191-2607(91)90145-G); no observed value was taken from it.

name: pocket_length_m
meaning: Turn pockets on approaches of two lanes or more, in metres per lane, split among the approach's movements: a vehicle passes those ahead of it that wait for another movement, as long as they fit in their pockets. 0 turns pockets off (every link one first-in-first-out queue).
source: An assumption: design guides size a bay from its expected queue, so no single length was found.

name: node_inflow
meaning: At the point queue only (flow level 2, and the point-queue warm-up loadings of levels 3 and 4), 1 makes a vehicle's entry onto the next link wait for that link's inflow headway, so a bottleneck's queue forms at the downstream end of the links feeding it; 0, the classic point queue, lets the next link take every vehicle at once, a link's outflow bounded by its own discharge capacity alone. 0 or 1. No effect at levels 3 and 4.
source: Uncalibrated: off, the point queue of Vickrey (1969), Congestion theory and transport investment, American Economic Review 59(2) 251–260, URL to add; on, an inflow headway at every node.

name: origin_inflow
meaning: 1: a departing vehicle enters its first link no faster than the link's inflow headway allows, as from an upstream link; 0: departures enter at any rate, so those given the same second (demand in departure bins) enter as one platoon. 0 or 1, at every flow level.
source: Uncalibrated: off. On treats the origin as a centroid connector with the first link's capacity, an assumption.

name: reroute_tree_s
meaning: How long, in seconds, one search tree grown from where a vehicle meets a closed link serves the next vehicles offered a route there (each by its own destination, on the link times of the moment the tree was grown); a vehicle offered one later gets a new tree. Where the route cost weighs more than time each offer is its own search. 0: a tree for every offer.
source: Uncalibrated: 60 s, an assumption: the queue's estimate changes little within a minute.

name: period_s
meaning: At flow level 1 only: the length of the period the demand departs over, in seconds, which its hourly flows are of (a link's flow is the PCU routed over it divided by this period in hours). 0 reads it from the departures: from the earliest, rounded down to the quarter hour, to the end of the quarter hour of the latest.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

meaning: At flow level 1 only: the α of the volume-delay function of a `living_street` road, in place of `bpr_alpha` (every class's) for this class.
source: The Bureau of Public Roads (1964), Traffic Assignment Manual, US Department of Commerce, URL to add; the value TNTP's benchmark networks use (https://github.com/bstabler/TransportationNetworks). Uncalibrated.

name: living_street.bpr_beta
meaning: At flow level 1 only: the β of the volume-delay function of a `living_street` road, in place of `bpr_beta` (every class's) for this class.
source: The Bureau of Public Roads (1964), Traffic Assignment Manual, US Department of Commerce, URL to add; the value TNTP's benchmark networks use (https://github.com/bstabler/TransportationNetworks). Uncalibrated.

name: service.bpr_alpha
meaning: At flow level 1 only: the α of the volume-delay function of a `service` road, in place of `bpr_alpha` (every class's) for this class.
source: The Bureau of Public Roads (1964), Traffic Assignment Manual, US Department of Commerce, URL to add; the value TNTP's benchmark networks use (https://github.com/bstabler/TransportationNetworks). Uncalibrated.

name: service.bpr_beta
meaning: At flow level 1 only: the β of the volume-delay function of a `service` road, in place of `bpr_beta` (every class's) for this class.
source: The Bureau of Public Roads (1964), Traffic Assignment Manual, US Department of Commerce, URL to add; the value TNTP's benchmark networks use (https://github.com/bstabler/TransportationNetworks). Uncalibrated.

name: walk_max_s
meaning: The longest walk, in seconds, that mode choice offers to a trip choosing its mode; a trip whose mode is given walks at any length. A traveller class may give its own.
source: Uncalibrated: a 30-minute cut-off for a whole trip on foot. England's average walking trip took 18 minutes in 2022 (Department for Transport, Walking factsheet 2022, https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/64e71a3d20ae89000df26d2b/walking-factsheet-2022.pdf).

name: bike_max_s
meaning: The longest ride, in seconds, that mode choice offers as a bike alternative to a trip choosing its mode; a trip whose mode is given rides at any length. A traveller class may give its own.
source: Uncalibrated: 60 minutes. About 80 % of Dutch bicycle trips are under 5 km (KiM, Cycling facts: new insights, 2020, https://english.kimnet.nl/documents/2020/11/03/cycling-facts-new-insights); the limit keeps the longer ones, e-bikes' among them.

name: fallback_car
meaning: 1: a trip left with no alternative at all (no mode it may use reaches its destination within the limits) travels by car instead, counted and reported apart; for a traveller without a car the car stands for a lift or a taxi. 0 leaves such trips unsimulated. 0 or 1.
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: car_access_s
meaning: The time a car trip takes before its drive — reaching the car and setting off — in seconds: added to a car alternative's door-to-door time and its walk in mode choice, and to the drive to a park-and-ride car park. 0 switches it off.
source: Uncalibrated: 120 s, an assumption with no published source.

name: car_egress_s
meaning: The time a car trip takes after its drive — finding a place and walking from it — in seconds: added to a car alternative's door-to-door time and its parking time in mode choice; a park-and-ride drive pays its car park's own time instead. 0 switches it off.
source: Uncalibrated: 180 s, an assumption. Cruising for parking alone averaged 8 minutes in sixteen downtown studies (Shoup 2006, Cruising for parking, Transport Policy 13(6), 479–486, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tranpol.2006.05.005), far above a city-wide mean that counts home and workplace parking.

name: bike_access_s
meaning: The time a bike trip takes before its ride — reaching and unlocking the bike — in seconds: paid at the departure and when the bike is fetched from a bike parking, in mode choice (as walk time) and in the loading. 0 switches it off.
source: Uncalibrated: 60 s, an assumption with no published source.

name: bike_egress_s
meaning: The time a bike trip takes after its ride — parking and locking the bike — in seconds: paid wherever a bike is left, at the destination and at a bike parking alike (a bike parking adds its occupancy's time, `parking_options` `slope_bike_s`), in mode choice (as parking time) and in the loading. 0 switches it off.
source: Uncalibrated: 60 s, an assumption with no published source.

name: car_snap_motorway_m
meaning: How close to a motorway-only node a trip's end must lie to join the roads there, in metres. A trip's end snaps to the nearest street node (one with a road a car can enter from; motorways, trunk roads and their ramps are not), unless it lies within this distance of a node that has only such roads, which it then takes. Read by every car trip. 0 sends every trip to a street; inf takes the nearest drivable node of any class.
source: Uncalibrated: 50 m, an assumption (a through trip placed on its motorway node lies at 0 m; an address is never within 50 m of a carriageway's node). No published source.

name: board_slack_s
meaning: How long before a vehicle leaves a passenger must be at the stop to board it, in seconds, at every boarding (a whole number).
source: An assumption: one minute to reach the platform and the door. Routing engines differ: OpenTripPlanner's boardSlack defaults to 0 (https://docs.opentripplanner.org/en/latest/RouteRequest/).

name: max_rides
meaning: The most vehicles one journey takes (eight rides is seven changes).
source: A resource limit, not behaviour: far beyond the journeys anyone makes in a city.

name: access_walk_max_s
meaning: The longest walk from an origin to a stop, or from a stop to a destination, in seconds (1 800 s is 2.4 km at walking speed): a choice-set limit, not a preference, since the choice model weighs the minutes walked. A traveller class may give its own.
source: An assumption. In Montréal the 85th percentile of the walk to a stop is about 524 m for buses and 1 259 m for commuter rail (El-Geneidy et al. 2014, Transportation 41(1) 193–210, https://ideas.repec.org/a/kap/transp/v41y2014i1p193-210.html): the limit leaves room for the few who walk further.

name: journey_max_s
meaning: The longest a journey with transit may take door to door, in seconds, to be offered: a longer one is no alternative. A choice-set limit, not a preference.
source: An assumption: two hours is more than a city's morning trip by transit takes.

name: transfer_walk_max_s
meaning: The longest walk between two stops in a change, in seconds (300 s is 400 m).
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: stop_walk_snap_m
meaning: The farthest a stop may be from the walk layer's nearest node, in metres, to be reached on foot; a stop farther away is treated as outside the study area.
source: An assumption: the layers' nodes are junctions, so a stop mid-block can be half a block from the nearest.

name: stop_transfer_s
meaning: The time a transfer at a stop takes between its access points (walk, bike and platform), in seconds.
source: Zero by construction: the walk to the platform is the walk leg's, and the margin before boarding is `board_slack_s`.

name: buses_on_roads
meaning: 1: every bus pattern the roads can carry rides them among the cars, and its passengers ride the times the loading gives it; 0: buses keep to the timetable and traffic never delays them. Travellers plan on the timetable either way. The `bus_` parameters act only with buses on the roads. 0 or 1.
source: A modelling choice, not a calibrated value: off, the timetable taken to hold the delays buses meet.

name: bus_dwell_s
meaning: How long a bus stays at each stop, in seconds; a dwelling bus does not block the traffic behind it.
source: An assumption standing for a typical stop: a bus's dwell depends mostly on its boardings and alightings (Dueker et al. 2004, Journal of Public Transportation 7(1) 21–40, https://doi.org/10.5038/2375-0901.7.1.2).

name: bus_pcu
meaning: How many passenger car units a bus counts for on the roads.
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: bus_plausibility_ratio
meaning: A bus pattern whose free-flow time on the roads, stop to stop, exceeds its scheduled time by more than this factor runs by the schedule instead of on the roads.
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: bus_stop_snap_m
meaning: The farthest a bus stop may be from the road network's nearest node, in metres, for its buses to ride the roads; a pattern with a stop farther away runs by the schedule.
source: An assumption, as for `stop_walk_snap_m`.

name: walk_max_s
meaning: The longest walk from a parking to a stop, in seconds (300 s is 400 m); a parking with no stop within it is left out.
source: An assumption, the same as the longest walk between stops.

name: reach_car_s
meaning: The longest drive to a park-and-ride car park, in seconds.
source: An assumption: 30 minutes; no published drive-time catchment was found.

name: reach_bike_s
meaning: The longest ride to a bike parking for bike-and-ride, in seconds of the bike layer's cost (its time with the mixed-traffic and lane factors).
source: An assumption: 20 minutes; most bike-and-ride users ride 2–5 km to their stop (Martens 2004, Transportation Research Part D 9(4) 281–294, https://www.worldtransitresearch.info/research/2043).

name: candidates
meaning: How many parkings a park-and-ride or bike-and-ride trip weighs: this many best by an estimate of the whole trip, and this many nearest by drive or ride time, so up to twice as many are tried.
source: A resource limit, and an assumption about how many stations a traveller weighs.

name: rank_speed_km_h
meaning: The speed, in km/h, a candidate parking's remaining straight-line distance to the destination is divided by to estimate the whole trip and rank candidates before they are tried.
source: A ranking device, not behaviour: about a tram's or a train's average speed.

name: slope_car_s
meaning: The time a car park full for a whole time bin adds to parking, in seconds (linear in the share of the bin it was full). Choice sees the availability expected from the iterations so far; a traveller pays the realised one.
source: An assumption: searching for a space, which studies of cruising for kerb parking put at several minutes (reviewed by Shoup 2006, Transport Policy 13(6) 479–486, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tranpol.2006.05.005).

name: slope_bike_s
meaning: The time a bike parking full for a whole time bin adds to parking, in seconds.
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: snap_m
meaning: The farthest a parking may be from its layers' nearest node, in metres.
source: An assumption, as for a stop.

name: bin_s
meaning: The length of the time bins, in seconds, in which each parking's availability is measured (and `parking_bins.parquet` is written).
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: pr_min_km
meaning: The shortest trip, in km as the crow flies, that mode choice offers park-and-ride and bike-and-ride to; a trip given one of those modes takes it at any length.
source: For computation, and an assumption: nobody drives to a car park for a 1 km trip. Uncalibrated.

name: reach_car_step_s
meaning: For computation: 0 searches each park-and-ride trip's drive to the car parks at its own departure; above 0, trips leaving one road node within one step of this many seconds share one search made at the step's middle, each drive still timed at its own departure. Approximate.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: car_eur_km
meaning: What driving costs per km, in euros: the fuel a driver pays (`cost_running_eur` of a car leg). Weighed only by a choice model that reads money (`beta_cost_eur`).
source: Uncalibrated: 0, since having a car is access, which traveller classes give. Set your own to weigh fuel.

name: bike_eur_km
meaning: What riding one's own bike costs per km, in euros (`cost_running_eur` of a bike leg).
source: Uncalibrated: nothing, as most models assume.

name: fare_base_eur
meaning: A transit journey's fare, once per journey, in euros (part of `cost_fare_eur`).
source: Uncalibrated: 0, since holding a pass or paying the fare is access, which traveller classes give. A city's own, to weigh fares: a single ticket in Paris is 2.55 € in 2026 (https://www.iledefrance-mobilites.fr/tarifs-titre-de-transport-en-commun-2026), in Lyon 2.10 € in 2025 (https://www.lebonbon.fr/lyon/news/augmentation-prix-tcl-1er-janvier-2025/); Amsterdam's GVB charges 1.16 € plus 0.217 € per km in 2026 (Vervoerregio Amsterdam, note BBV/2025/15361, p. 2, https://vervoerregio.bestuurlijkeinformatie.nl/Document/View/abddeeb0-be54-4eae-9622-4ac0935df151).

name: fare_km_eur
meaning: A transit journey's fare per km ridden, in euros per km, the km counted from each boarding stop to its alighting stop as the crow flies.
source: Uncalibrated: 0, a flat fare.

name: fare_transfer_eur
meaning: A transit journey's fare per transfer, in euros (a new ticket at each boarding: set it to the base fare).
source: Uncalibrated: 0, transfers free within a journey.

name: parking_car_eur
meaning: A car park's fee per stay, in euros, where its parking table gives none; counted on the park-and-ride trip that parks, not on the one that fetches.
source: Uncalibrated: free.

name: parking_bike_eur
meaning: A bike parking's fee per stay, in euros, where its parking table gives none.
source: Uncalibrated: free.

name: increments
meaning: In how many groups of about equal size, a draw per traveller, the free-flow loading (iteration 0) is built up: the first group chooses on free-flow times, each next one on the times of a loading of the groups before it, until everyone has chosen. 1 lets everyone choose at once on free-flow times. No effect at flow level 0.
source: Uncalibrated: groups of a fifth of the travellers (incremental assignment); 5 when not given

name: warmup
meaning: How many of the first loadings, the free-flow loading's groups included, use the point-queue model, which cannot gridlock, in place of the run's flow level. The last loading of a run that iterates always uses the run's flow level.
source: A setting: 1 when not given.

name: gap_tolerance
meaning: At flow level 1: stop once the relative gap of the flows, (Σ x t − Σ d t_min) / Σ d t_min, is below this; 0 never stops early. From 0 to 1.
source: A common target of static assignment: Boyce, Ralevic-Dekic and Bar-Gera (2004), Convergence of traffic assignments: how much is enough?, Journal of Transportation Engineering 130(1) 49–55, URL to add, argue for 1e-4 or below.

name: iterations
meaning: At flow level 1: the most Frank–Wolfe iterations; it may stop earlier at `gap_tolerance`.
source: Uncalibrated: about what Sioux Falls at TNTP's demand takes to reach the default tolerance.

name: cost_bin_s
meaning: The length, in seconds, of the time bins in which link times are recorded for the next choice; shorter follows a queue more closely and takes more memory.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: gap_every
meaning: 1: the full gap in the choice model's currency is measured after every loading; 0: after the last loading alone. 0 or 1.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: gap_sample
meaning: How many trips are tested against the whole network (a fastest-route search at the last loading's times) at the last iteration, for the network gap; 0 for none.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: gap_tolerance
meaning: Stop iterating once the disequilibrium (the gap less what the choice model itself expects; the worse of the routes' and the itinerary trips'), averaged over the last three iterations, is below this share, and only from the fourth loading on; 0 never stops early. From 0 to 1.
source: Uncalibrated: 0.05 is the convergence verdict's "good" (0.15 "acceptable").

name: increments
meaning: In how many groups of about equal size, a draw per traveller, the free-flow loading (iteration 0) is built up: the first group chooses on free-flow times, each next one on the times of a loading of the groups before it, until everyone has chosen. 1 lets everyone choose at once on free-flow times. No effect at flow level 0.
source: Uncalibrated: groups of a fifth of the travellers (incremental assignment); 5 when not given

name: itinerary_gap_sample
meaning: How many transit, park-and-ride and bike-and-ride trips, besides those choosing again, plan their whole choice set after each loading to measure the itinerary gap; the default, 100 000 000, means every trip. Fewer is faster but makes the gap before the last iteration read low; the last iteration always plans every trip.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: iterations
meaning: The most loadings an `msa` run makes; it may stop earlier at `gap_tolerance`. At iteration i a share 1 / (i + 1) of the travellers, a draw per traveller, chooses again on the last loading's times.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: route_growth_tolerance
meaning: A run may stop at `gap_tolerance` only while the last route update added routes for at most this share of the pairs it searched; 1 lets the gap alone decide. From 0 to 1.
source: A setting: 1 when not given; 0 stops no run while the update adds any route.

name: warmup
meaning: How many of the first loadings, the free-flow loading's groups included, use the point-queue model, which cannot gridlock, in place of the run's flow level. The last loading of a run that iterates always uses the run's flow level.
source: A setting: 1 when not given.

name: cost_bin_s
meaning: The length, in seconds, of the time bins in which link times are recorded for the next choice; shorter follows a queue more closely and takes more memory.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: eta_fell
meaning: How much η grows after a loading whose disequilibrium (the gap less what the choice model itself expects) fell below the loading's before it: the share choosing again, 1 / η, shrinks slowly while the run improves. From 0 to 1; with `eta_rose` also 1 it is `msa`.
source: Uncalibrated: 0.2, the value of Ma and He (2024); Liu, He and He (2009), Method of successive weighted averages (MSWA) and self-regulated averaging schemes for solving stochastic user equilibrium problem, Networks and Spatial Economics 9, 485–503, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11067-009-9108-9, tried 0.01 to 0.5.

name: eta_rose
meaning: How much η grows after a loading whose disequilibrium rose or stayed: the share choosing again, 1 / η, shrinks fast when the run does not improve. From 1 to 10.
source: Uncalibrated: 1.5, within the 1.5 to 2 that Liu, He and He (2009), Method of successive weighted averages (MSWA) and self-regulated averaging schemes for solving stochastic user equilibrium problem, Networks and Spatial Economics 9, 485–503, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11067-009-9108-9, tried; Ma and He (2024) used 1.1.

name: gap_every
meaning: 1: the full gap in the choice model's currency is measured after every loading; 0: after the last loading alone. 0 or 1.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: gap_sample
meaning: How many trips are tested against the whole network (a fastest-route search at the last loading's times) at the last iteration, for the network gap; 0 for none.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: gap_tolerance
meaning: Stop iterating once the disequilibrium (the gap less what the choice model itself expects; the worse of the routes' and the itinerary trips'), averaged over the last three iterations, is below this share, and only from the fourth loading on; 0 never stops early. From 0 to 1.
source: Uncalibrated: 0.05 is the convergence verdict's "good" (0.15 "acceptable").

name: increments
meaning: In how many groups of about equal size, a draw per traveller, the free-flow loading (iteration 0) is built up: the first group chooses on free-flow times, each next one on the times of a loading of the groups before it, until everyone has chosen. 1 lets everyone choose at once on free-flow times. No effect at flow level 0.
source: Uncalibrated: groups of a fifth of the travellers (incremental assignment); 5 when not given

name: itinerary_gap_sample
meaning: How many transit, park-and-ride and bike-and-ride trips, besides those choosing again, plan their whole choice set after each loading to measure the itinerary gap; the default, 100 000 000, means every trip. Fewer is faster but makes the gap before the last iteration read low; the last iteration always plans every trip.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: iterations
meaning: The most loadings an `sra` run makes; it may stop earlier at `gap_tolerance`. At iteration k a share 1 / η_k of the travellers, a draw per traveller, chooses again on the last loading's times; η_1 = 2, and η grows by `eta_fell` after a loading whose disequilibrium fell and by `eta_rose` after one where it rose.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: route_growth_tolerance
meaning: A run may stop at `gap_tolerance` only while the last route update added routes for at most this share of the pairs it searched; 1 lets the gap alone decide. From 0 to 1.
source: A setting: 1 when not given; 0 stops no run while the update adds any route.

name: warmup
meaning: How many of the first loadings, the free-flow loading's groups included, use the point-queue model, which cannot gridlock, in place of the run's flow level. The last loading of a run that iterates always uses the run's flow level.
source: A setting: 1 when not given.

name: max_attempts
meaning: The most searches for one origin–destination pair. Given `max_paths` alone, it becomes 3 × `max_paths`.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: max_detour
meaning: No route kept costs more than this multiple of the pair's best route's free-flow cost (at least 1).
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: max_overlap
meaning: A new route is kept only if it shares at most this share of its cost with each route kept before (above 0, at most 1).
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: max_paths
meaning: The most routes kept for one pair (1 to 32).
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: penalty
meaning: The factor the cost of the links of the route just found is multiplied by before searching again (above 1): larger pushes the next route further from the last.
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: draws
meaning: How many perturbed preference draws per user class, besides the unperturbed draw 0 (0 to 64): in each, the class's coefficients are drawn around their values and every link's cost is perturbed by `sigma`.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: max_detour
meaning: No route kept costs more than this multiple of the travel-time shortest route's cost, in the generalised cost it was searched by (at least 1).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: max_overlap
meaning: A new route is kept only if it shares at most this share of its generalised cost with each route kept before (above 0, at most 1).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: max_paths
meaning: The most routes kept for one pair (1 to 32).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: seed
meaning: Which draws are made: another value gives other link noise and other preference draws for every pair. Independent of `master_seed`.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: sigma
meaning: The link noise: from draw 1 on, a link's cost is multiplied by 1 + sigma × u, u a uniform draw from 0 to 1 (at least 0).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: tau
meaning: The spread of the preference draws: each of a class's coefficients is multiplied by 1 + tau × v, v a uniform draw from −1 to 1 (at least 0).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: max_paths
meaning: The most routes kept for one pair: the least-cost route and up to `max_paths` − 1 twins, routes that cost at most `twin_tolerance` more and leave the least-cost route once (1 to 8; 1 keeps the least-cost route alone).
source: A modelling choice: a twin lets the choice model split an exact tie (two equal ways round a block) that a least-cost search would settle by the order of the network's links. Uncalibrated.

name: twin_tolerance
meaning: How much more than the least cost a twin may cost, as a share (0 to 1; 0 keeps exact ties only).
source: Uncalibrated: 0.1 %, wide enough for costs equal but for rounding, narrow enough that a route a second longer on a ten-minute trip is not a twin.

name: biased
meaning: 1: a draw raises a link's cost in proportion to its propensity to congest, from the demand (the busiest half-hour's load on free-flow shortest routes over the link's capacity, clipped at 1); 0: every link alike.
source: A modelling choice: the simulation approach to choice-set generation with its noise where the demand is heavy. Unbiased noise measured worse on the one heavy load it was tried on.

name: draws
meaning: How many random cost draws to try for one pair (0 to 1 000).
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: max_detour
meaning: No route kept costs more than this multiple of the pair's best route's free-flow cost (at least 1).
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: max_overlap
meaning: A new route is kept only if it shares at most this share of its cost with each route kept before (above 0, at most 1).
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: max_paths
meaning: The most routes kept for one pair (1 to 32).
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: seed
meaning: Which draws are made: another value gives another set of draws for every pair. Independent of `master_seed`.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: sigma
meaning: How far a link's cost may rise in a draw: it is multiplied by 1 + sigma × u × bias, u a uniform draw from 0 to 1 (above 0).
source: An assumption; no published source.

name: draws
meaning: How many perturbed preference draws per iteration (0 to 16): each one perturbed search tree per origin, departure bin and user class, whose route to a pair is added if it is new and within `max_detour` of the set's best.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: max_detour
meaning: A drawn route is added only if its cost at the bin's middle, in its class's generalised cost for the draw, is at most this multiple of the set's best in that cost (at least 1).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: max_routes
meaning: The most routes a pair's set may hold (1 to 32). A full set is still searched: a route at least one second faster than the set's best replaces a route nobody chose in the last choice (never the free-flow shortest one); if every route is in use, it waits.
source: A setting: a set holds more routes than a traveller is offered (`choice_max_routes`).

name: searches
meaning: How many fastest-route searches per pair per iteration, at evenly spread quantiles of the pair's departures (1: the median). More finds routes that pay only at some hours, and makes bigger sets.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: seed
meaning: Which draws are made; each iteration draws afresh from it. Independent of `master_seed`.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: sigma
meaning: The link noise: a link's cost is multiplied by 1 + sigma × u, u a uniform draw from 0 to 1 (at least 0).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: slack
meaning: A pair is not searched while its set's best route at its departure is within this share of the route's free-flow time, since no route is faster than free flow: the regret left is at most this share. 0 searches every pair. From 0 to 1.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: tau
meaning: The spread of the preference draws: each coefficient but time's is multiplied by 1 + tau × v, v a uniform draw from −1 to 1 (at least 0).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: tree_step_s
meaning: Search trees: 0 searches each pair on its own, at its departures; above 0, departures are rounded to this step (in seconds) and the pairs of one origin at one rounded departure share one search tree, which finds each one's fastest route at once. Approximate (the routes are the fastest at the rounded departure) and much faster where many trips share an origin; the starter cases use 1 800.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: max_routes
meaning: The most routes a pair's set may hold (1 to 32). A full set is still searched: a route at least one second faster than the set's best replaces a route nobody chose in the last choice (never the free-flow shortest one); if every route is in use, it waits.
source: A setting: a set holds more routes than a traveller is offered (`choice_max_routes`).

name: searches
meaning: How many fastest-route searches per pair per iteration, at evenly spread quantiles of the pair's departures (1: the median). More finds routes that pay only at some hours, and makes bigger sets.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: slack
meaning: A pair is not searched while its set's best route at its departure is within this share of the route's free-flow time, since no route is faster than free flow: the regret left is at most this share. 0 searches every pair. From 0 to 1.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: tree_step_s
meaning: Search trees: 0 searches each pair on its own, at its departures; above 0, departures are rounded to this step (in seconds) and the pairs of one origin at one rounded departure share one search tree, which finds each one's fastest route at once. Approximate (the routes are the fastest at the rounded departure) and much faster where many trips share an origin; the starter cases use 1 800.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: until_iteration
meaning: The last iteration whose routes the update adds (0: every iteration). After it the sets stay as they are and the remaining loadings settle the choices among them, without the jumps a route added late causes when the few who choose again move to it.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: beta_bike_mixed_km
meaning: Weighs each km of a bike leg in mixed traffic, on top of its time, so a ride's route and its mode are chosen alike: at −0.16 it matches the bike route search's mixed-traffic factor (1.2) at the default time weight and bike speed.
source: An assumption, derived from the bike route search's defaults (0.8 minute more per km at 15 km/h, times −0.2).

name: beta_cost_eur
meaning: Weighs what an alternative costs, per euro (`cost_eur`). A value of time of V euros per hour is `beta_cost_eur = beta_time_min × 60 / V`; every shipped price is 0, so money weighs only the prices a scenario gives.
source: An assumption: a value of time of 10 € per hour at the default time weight.

name: beta_ln_path_size
meaning: Weighs the logarithm of the path-size factor: routes that share links with the others in the set split their share, which repairs the logit's blindness to overlap (the path-size logit).
source: The path-size term of Ben-Akiva and Bierlaire (1999)

name: beta_time_min
meaning: Weighs the expected travel time, per minute (door to door for an itinerary): the main term of the utility. At −0.2 a route four minutes slower is taken with about 45 % of the weight of one that is not.
source: An assumption, not a calibration.

name: beta_transfers
meaning: Weighs each change of vehicle, per transfer: −1 is about five minutes of riding at the default time weight.
source: An assumption, well below the 15.2–17.7 minutes of riding Garcia-Martinez et al. (2018), Transportation Research Part A 114 52–66, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tra.2018.01.016, estimate in Madrid.

name: beta_wait_min
meaning: Weighs minutes waiting at stops on top of `time_min`, so a minute waited weighs about 1.45 times a minute riding at the default time weight.
source: Wardman (2004), Transport Policy 11(4) 363–377, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tranpol.2004.05.001: waiting weighs on average 1.47 times in-vehicle time.

name: beta_walk_min
meaning: Weighs minutes walking on top of `time_min`, so a minute walked weighs about 1.65 times a minute riding at the default time weight. 0 for a car route.
source: Wardman (2004), Transport Policy 11(4) 363–377, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tranpol.2004.05.001: walking weighs on average 1.66 times in-vehicle time in British evidence (which the author finds too low).

name: mu
meaning: The nest scale, above 0 and at most 1: the alternatives of one mode share a nest, and a smaller mu makes them closer substitutes for each other than for the other modes, so a mode with several routes does not gain share from their number. 1 is the flat logit.
source: An assumption: no published range was found for route-in-mode nests.

name: beta_bike_mixed_km
meaning: Weighs each km of a bike leg in mixed traffic, on top of its time, so a ride's route and its mode are chosen alike: at −0.16 it matches the bike route search's mixed-traffic factor (1.2) at the default time weight and bike speed.
source: An assumption, derived from the bike route search's defaults (0.8 minute more per km at 15 km/h, times −0.2).

name: beta_cost_eur
meaning: Weighs what an alternative costs, per euro (`cost_eur`). A value of time of V euros per hour is `beta_cost_eur = beta_time_min × 60 / V`; every shipped price is 0, so money weighs only the prices a scenario gives.
source: An assumption: a value of time of 10 € per hour at the default time weight.

name: beta_ln_path_size
meaning: Weighs the logarithm of the path-size factor: routes that share links with the others in the set split their share, which repairs the logit's blindness to overlap (the path-size logit).

meaning: Weighs the expected travel time, per minute (door to door for an itinerary): the main term of the utility. At −0.2 a route four minutes slower is taken with about 45 % of the weight of one that is not.
source: An assumption, not a calibration.

name: beta_transfers
meaning: Weighs each change of vehicle, per transfer: −1 is about five minutes of riding at the default time weight.
source: An assumption, well below the 15.2–17.7 minutes of riding Garcia-Martinez et al. (2018), Transportation Research Part A 114 52–66, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tra.2018.01.016, estimate in Madrid.

name: beta_wait_min
meaning: Weighs minutes waiting at stops on top of `time_min`, so a minute waited weighs about 1.45 times a minute riding at the default time weight.

meaning: Weighs minutes walking on top of `time_min`, so a minute walked weighs about 1.65 times a minute riding at the default time weight. 0 for a car route.

name: draws
meaning: How many perturbed preference draws per user class, besides the unperturbed draw 0 (0 to 64): in each, the class's coefficients are drawn around their values and every link's cost is perturbed by `sigma`.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: max_detour
meaning: No route kept costs more than this multiple of the travel-time shortest route's cost, in the generalised cost it was searched by (at least 1).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: max_overlap
meaning: A new route is kept only if it shares at most this share of its generalised cost with each route kept before (above 0, at most 1).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: max_paths
meaning: The most bike routes kept for one pair (1 to 32).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: seed
meaning: Which draws are made: another value gives other link noise and other preference draws for every pair. Independent of `master_seed`.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: sigma
meaning: The link noise: from draw 1 on, a link's cost is multiplied by 1 + sigma × u, u a uniform draw from 0 to 1 (at least 0).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: tau
meaning: The spread of the preference draws: each of a class's coefficients is multiplied by 1 + tau × v, v a uniform draw from −1 to 1 (at least 0).
source: The method of Bovy and Fiorenzo-Catalano (2007), Stochastic route choice set generation: behavioral and probabilistic foundations, Transportmetrica 3(3) 173–189, https://doi.org/10.1080/18128600708685672; the value is uncalibrated.

name: walk_max_s
meaning: The longest walk to a dock from the origin, or from a dock to the destination, in seconds on the walk layer.
source: Uncalibrated: 600 s is about 800 m; bike-sharing catchments of 300–500 m are commonly assumed (citation to add).

name: candidates
meaning: The most dock pairs (pickup, return) one trip chooses among; three times as many pairs are estimated first.
source: A resource limit, as the parkings' `candidates`; no source needed.

name: snap_m
meaning: The farthest a dock may be from its layers' nearest node, in metres; a dock farther away is left out.
source: An assumption, as for a parking.

name: redirect_max
meaning: The most other docks a traveller tries when the dock they reach has no bike (at the pickup) or no free slot (at the return).
source: Uncalibrated: about three, an assumption (citation to add).

name: redirect_max_m
meaning: How far from the dock they planned a traveller looks for another, in metres as the crow flies.
source: Uncalibrated: about 800 m, an assumption (citation to add).

name: pickup_s
meaning: The time to take a bike from a dock, in seconds.
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption (citation to add).

name: return_s
meaning: The time to dock a bike, in seconds.
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption (citation to add).

name: ride_factor
meaning: A shared bike's ride time over the bike layer's, for the whole fleet: 1 rides as one's own bike; below 1, a faster fleet such as e-bikes (above 0).
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption.

name: start_share
meaning: The share of a dock's slots holding a bike when the day starts, where the dock's row gives no count (an OpenStreetMap dock). From 0 to 1.
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption.

name: fail_s
meaning: What finding no bike near a dock costs a pickup in the travellers' choice, in seconds: the assumed cost of walking on or taking another mode, where the docks' assumed counts leave no bike.
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption (citation to add).

name: bin_s
meaning: The length, in seconds, of the time bins in which the docks' counts and the travellers' assumed costs at the docks are kept (above 0).
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: handling_s
meaning: The time an operator's move takes per bike, loading and unloading, in seconds, on top of the van's drive.
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption (citation to add).

name: van_bikes
meaning: The most bikes an operator's van carries in one move (at least 1).
source: Uncalibrated: a small van or a bike trailer, an assumption (citation to add).

name: log_events
meaning: 1 keeps the service day's log of events (every arrival at a dock, bike taken, dock found empty or full, walk or ride on, return and arrival at the destination: `bike_share_events.parquet`); 0 keeps none, for a very large run, whose results are otherwise the same. 0 or 1. A switch of what is kept, not of what is simulated: not in the run's fingerprint.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: battery_kwh
meaning: A vehicle's usable battery, in kWh.
source: Uncalibrated: a mid-size electric car's usable battery, an assumption.

name: kwh_per_km
meaning: A vehicle's energy use per kilometre driven, in kWh.
source: Uncalibrated: urban driving of a mid-size electric car, an assumption.

name: soc_start
meaning: A vehicle's charge when the day starts, as a share of its battery, where its row gives none.
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption.

name: reserve_soc
meaning: The charge a vehicle keeps after a trip, as a share of its battery: a vehicle whose drive to a request and the ride would end below it is not sent (room to reach a charger).
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption.

name: charge_below
meaning: The fleet's own charging rule: a vehicle that drops a passenger with its charge below this share of its battery drives to the nearest charger.
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption.

name: charge_to
meaning: The share of its battery a vehicle charges to.
source: Uncalibrated: charging slows above about 80 %, an assumption.

name: charger_kw
meaning: A charger's power per plug, in kW, where its row gives none.
source: Uncalibrated: a fast charger's, an assumption.

name: request_cancel_s
meaning: A request is cancelled if no taxi can pick it up within this time, in seconds, from the request to the taxi reaching the pickup, the dispatch delay included; the trip then ends there.
source: Uncalibrated: 600 s, an assumption (citation to add).

name: boarding_s
meaning: The time to get in at the pickup, in seconds.
source: Uncalibrated: 60 s, an assumption.

name: dispatch_delay_s
meaning: The time from a request being matched to a taxi to the taxi setting off to the pickup, in seconds (the dispatch and the driver's acceptance); the taxi is held for the request meanwhile and drives no kilometre. Below `request_cancel_s` (or both 0).
source: Uncalibrated: 120 s, an assumption (citation to add).

name: snap_m
meaning: The farthest a vehicle or charger may be from the road network, in metres.
source: An assumption, as for docks and parkings.

name: charger_reach_s
meaning: How far, in seconds of free-flow driving, a vehicle looks for its nearest charger; one with none in reach does not charge.
source: Uncalibrated: an hour's drive covers a city, an assumption.

name: log_events
meaning: 1 keeps the service day's log of events (every request, vehicle sent, pickup, drop-off, cancellation and charge, with the vehicle's state and charge after each: `taxi_events.parquet`); 0 keeps none, for a very large run, whose results are otherwise the same. 0 or 1. A switch of what is kept, not of what is simulated: not in the run's fingerprint.
source: A setting of the computation, not a behavioural value; no source needed.

name: assumed_wait_s
meaning: The waiting time travellers assume, when choosing, before a taxi picks them up, in seconds: the same for every request, whatever the fleet's `request_cancel_s`. What the fleet actually gives is the service day's.
source: Uncalibrated: 600 s, an assumption (citation to add).

name: assumed_no_taxi_share
meaning: The chance of getting no taxi that travellers assume when choosing, from 0 to 1 (a request cancelled because no taxi could pick it up in time).
source: Uncalibrated: 0, an assumption.

name: assumed_extra_walk_at_pickup_s
meaning: The extra walk a shared-bike user assumes, when choosing, if the pickup dock is empty, in seconds, the same at every dock and time bin. Not set: assumed from the docks' start-of-day bikes, dock by dock and bin by bin.
source: Uncalibrated: the start-of-day bikes, an assumption.

name: assumed_extra_walk_at_return_s
meaning: The extra walk a shared-bike user assumes, when choosing, if the return dock is full, in seconds, the same at every dock and time bin. Not set: assumed from the docks' start-of-day bikes, dock by dock and bin by bin.
source: Uncalibrated: the start-of-day bikes, an assumption.

name: bike_share_eur_per_ride
meaning: A shared bike's fare per ride, in euros.
source: Uncalibrated: 0, free, until a study sets its service's fare.

name: bike_share_eur_per_min
meaning: A shared bike's fare per minute ridden, in euros.
source: Uncalibrated: 0, free, until a study sets its service's fare.

name: taxi_eur_per_ride
meaning: A taxi's fare per ride, in euros (with `taxi_eur_per_km`, or a mode constant, needed for a taxi to be offered).
source: Uncalibrated: 0, until a study sets its fleet's fare.

name: taxi_eur_per_km
meaning: A taxi's fare per kilometre ridden, in euros.
source: Uncalibrated: 0, until a study sets its fleet's fare.

name: step_s
meaning: The time between the steps of the operator that decides nothing, in seconds: the day is the day without an operator, stepped (for comparing a policy with doing nothing at the same steps).
source: Uncalibrated: 900 s, an assumption.

name: step_s
meaning: The time between the operator's steps in the service day, in seconds: at each step it looks at the services and decides.
source: Uncalibrated: 900 s, an assumption.

name: from_s
meaning: The second of the day from which the operator moves every dock back toward its count at the start of the day.
source: Uncalibrated: 0, from the start, an assumption.

name: low
meaning: A dock holding fewer bikes than this share of its slots is topped up to the middle of `low` and `high`.
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption.

name: high
meaning: A dock holding more bikes than this share of its slots gives bikes away down to the middle of `low` and `high`.
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption.

name: step_s
meaning: The time between the operator's steps in the service day, in seconds: at each step it looks at the services and decides.
source: Uncalibrated: 900 s, an assumption.

name: charge_below
meaning: At each step, an idle taxi charged below this share of its battery is sent to the charger nearest it (besides the fleet's own charging rule).
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption.

name: charge_to
meaning: The share of its battery a taxi the operator sends to charge charges to.
source: Uncalibrated: an assumption.

name: step_s
meaning: The time between the operator's steps in the service day, in seconds: at each step it looks at the services and decides.
source: Uncalibrated: 900 s, an assumption.

meaning: Weighs a route's length in km (an itinerary's car or bike leg's), per km.
source: No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility.

name: beta_detour
meaning: Weighs an alternative's time over the best alternative's, minus one, per unit.
source: No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility.

source: No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility.

name: beta_cost_running_eur
meaning: Weighs the car or bike leg's km at the vehicle's price per km, in euros, per euro.
source: No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility.

name: beta_cost_toll_eur
meaning: Weighs the car leg's tolls (a road link value named `toll_eur`), in euros, per euro.
source: No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility.

name: beta_cost_parking_eur
meaning: Weighs the parking fee, in euros: a park-and-ride or bike-and-ride parking's, on the trip that parks, or the trip's destination's for one arriving by car, per euro.
source: No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility.

name: beta_cost_fare_eur

name: beta_trip_departure_h
meaning: Weighs the trip's departure in hours after midnight. Being the same for every alternative of a choice, it changes no probability on its own; it weighs in a product with another attribute, `beta_<a>*<b>`.
source: No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility.

name: beta_mode_walk
meaning: The constant of the `walk` mode: weighs the attribute that is 1 for a walk alternative, 0 otherwise. Weighed on top of the time, it shifts the mode's share in mode choice.
source: No default weight: 0 leaves the attribute out of the utility.

name: w_cancelled
meaning: The standard reward's weight per person whose request was cancelled (a taxi request no taxi could pick up in time, or a shared-bike traveller who found no bike).
source: Uncalibrated: named so a study sets its own.

name: w_wait

name: w_walk

name: w_km

name: zone_grid_m
meaning: The side, in metres, of the square zones an operator's view groups places by (`fleet_day`, `fleet_environment`).
